prompt: A fresh heap has one free block of payload 480 bytes. `sizeof(Block)` is 32, sizes round up to 16, and a block is split only if `size >= want + 32 + 16`. Run `a = kmalloc(50); b = kmalloc(300); c = kmalloc(40);`, then `kfree(a); kfree(b);`.

trace.label: [payload size] of the free block after `kmalloc(50)`
[payload size] of the free block after `kmalloc(300)`
`kmalloc(40)` wants 48 and the free block has 48: payload size handed out
After the two frees, the merged free block's payload size

explain: kmalloc(50) rounds to 64; 480 >= 64 + 48, so the block splits and the leftover has 480 - 64 - 32 = 384 (the new header eats 32). kmalloc(300) rounds to 304 and leaves 384 - 304 - 32 = 48. kmalloc(40) wants 48 and the block has exactly 48, which is below 48 + 48, so no split: the whole block is used and no free bytes remain. Freeing a and b (adjacent) merges them: the second header becomes payload, so 64 + 32 + 304 = 400. Block c stays used and blocks any merge beyond it.
